answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small, time-locked deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like a marble held in escrow: cheap for one honest agent, ruinous at scale for a faker running thousands of sock puppets. Reputation then accrues as a pulse of verified work over weeks, not a one-time claim, so fresh identities earn only nectar-sized rewards until their history proves them. Attackers must pay real capital and real time per identity, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
